name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.27.0 (released 2026-08-04) is the latest release, adding email-based login, hardening message templating against memory exhaustion (limiting templates to 32 KB, printf widths, and indent depth), and graduating PostgreSQL support out of experimental status. Recent releases also introduced password reset via magic links (v2.25.0), CPU DoS protection for message templates (v2.26.0), and an abuse ban-feed for fail2ban integration (v2.26.3). Active development is ongoing with horizontal clustering in progress. Full release notes: https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (client) — check repository for details; not explicitly stated in changelog
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in 2026, active bug fixes, security patches, and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — username/password auth, access tokens, email-based login, topic reservations, and configurable default access policies (e.g. deny-all)
answers.Is there a hosted cloud version availabl: Yes — ntfy.sh is the official hosted cloud instance

breaking_excerpts: Message cache databases from ntfy older than v1.10.0 (November 2021) can no longer be migrated; upgrade via an older ntfy version first, or delete the cache database.
X-Email: yes now requires being logged in with a verified primary email address; previously it was rejected unless smtp-sender-verify was enabled — behavior has changed.
Web app dependency major-version upgrades: Vite 6→8 (Rolldown-based), Material UI 5→9, Dexie 3→4 — may affect self-hosted web app builds or customizations.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise is a powerful multi-platform notification library supporting dozens of services, but it is a library/CLI tool rather than a standalone pub-sub server like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet adds file sharing and link mirroring between devices but is a closed-source cloud service with a limited free tier and no self-hosting capability.

alternatives.name: Ntopng / Alertmanager (Prometheus)
alternatives.review: Alertmanager is purpose-built for infrastructure alerting with rich routing and grouping rules, but it is narrowly scoped to metrics-based alerts rather than general-purpose pub-sub notifications.
